sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test tool imports
sections.what: Brings in the browser automation tool, the test runner functions, the development server builder and the project model type.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A missing browser install makes setup fail before any check runs.

sections.name: model
sections.title: Fake saved model used in tests
sections.what: Defines a small made-up building model with one foundation element. The browser tests hand this to the app in place of a real saved file, so the tests run on known data.
sections.why: The comment says these are synthetic responses and never real user artifacts. Using fake data keeps the tests repeatable and keeps user files out of them.
sections.watch_out: If the real model format changes, this fake model may stop matching it and the tests can fail for the wrong reason.

sections.name: scene
sections.title: Fake programme scene used in tests
sections.what: Builds a made-up schedule view data set that wraps the same single element. The programme page loads this data during the tests.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond supplying the programme page with data that matches the fake model.
sections.watch_out: The activity lists are empty, so these tests do not check how activity labels appear.

sections.name: TestState
sections.title: Test server, browser and shared state
sections.what: Before any test runs, starts a local development server and a Chromium browser. After all tests, it closes both. The TestState type describes the bookkeeping the tests keep inside the page: the chosen failure mode, how many times the 3D setup was tried, and copies of saved responses.
sections.why: A real browser is needed because only a real browser can start WebGL. The launch flags ask the browser to use software graphics, which is likely so the tests run on machines without a graphics card.
sections.watch_out: Starting the browser has a 60 second limit, so a slow machine could fail here before any test runs. The Chromium path is used only if a local copy exists.

sections.name: newPage
sections.title: Open a fresh browser page
sections.what: Creates a new blank browser tab for a test and fails clearly if the browser did not start.
sections.why: Each test gets its own tab so one test's state does not leak into another.
sections.watch_out: Each test must close its tab. The tests do this in finally blocks, so a failure still closes the tab.

sections.name: openSaved
sections.title: Open saved model with controlled failures
sections.what: Opens the app in a test tab with fake server replies. It also injects code that forces WebGL setup to fail in a chosen way, records a copy of each saved response, and records every error and every API request. Any API address not expected by the test causes an error.
sections.why: The tests must force WebGL failures on purpose and then prove that saved data was not changed by the recovery.
sections.watch_out: The injected code replaces built-in browser functions for the whole page, so it could change behavior elsewhere if a test adds more code to it.

sections.name: assertSavedUnchanged
sections.title: Check saved data was not changed
sections.what: Confirms that every saved response recorded during the test still matches its original text, and that at least one was recorded.
sections.why: This backs the warning shown to users that retrying does not alter their saved model.
sections.watch_out: The check passes only if responses were recorded, so a broken recording step would show up as a failure rather than a silent pass.

sections.name: WebGL initialization in the real application (including StrictMode) (part 1)
sections.title: Failure, retry and normal view tests
sections.what: For both the project view and the programme view, the first test checks that the warning box appears with its explanation, that End opens the 3D view, that Retry restarts only the 3D view without new downloads, and that recovery shows one visible element with no errors. The second test checks that a working 3D view renders normally with no warning.
sections.why: These tests check the promises made in the warning text against the real app in a real browser.
sections.watch_out: The test waits a fixed 200 milliseconds to confirm no automatic retry happens. On a slow machine this wait may be too short to catch a retry.

sections.name: WebGL initialization in the real application (including StrictMode) (part 2)
sections.title: Back to start without reloading or uploading
sections.what: Checks that the Back to start link returns to the file upload screen, clears the page address hash, makes only GET requests, records no errors, and leaves saved data unchanged.
sections.why: The warning promises that going back does not upload or regenerate anything, and this test checks that promise.
sections.watch_out: The link appears only when a home address is passed to the boundary, so this test depends on that setting.
